title: Two algorithms from their pages
description:
Write `accumulate` and `count_if` from their descriptions.

```
accumulate({1, 2, 3, 4}, 0) = 10
accumulate({"a", "b", "c"}, std::string{}) = "abc"
count_if({1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, even) = 3
```
hints: The return type is `T`, the type of `init`, so `0` makes it add as `int` even for a vector of `double` (lesson 1.03).
`count_if` returns `typename std::iterator_traits<It>::difference_type`, which is why the page shows that long name.
requirements: Write your own first. cppreference pages end with a "Possible implementation" section (lesson 2.01 tours the rest of the page): look at it only afterwards, to compare.
Match the signatures (template parameters, the value returned).
Note in a comment what the page says about the initial value's type and why `accumulate(v, 0)` with doubles loses the fractions.
stretch: Write `std::transform_reduce`'s simplest overload the same way.
